# Progress: `jl-progress`

A bar that shows how much of a task is done, or that work goes on.

- Class `JlProgress`, an atom: `import { JlProgress } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/progress

A progress bar shows how much of a task is done, when the page knows it: an upload, an import, a quota.
Without a value, the bar runs back and forth: the work goes on, its end is unknown.

It is a progressbar for screen readers, named by its label (or "Progress"), with its value as a percentage. Keep the
accent while work runs; use the semantic tones for what a level means, such as a quota nearly full.

## Use

```ts
import { JlProgress } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlProgress label="Uploading report.pdf" showValue value={64} />
```

```html
<jl-progress label="Uploading report.pdf" show-value value="64"></jl-progress>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `value` (attribute `value`): `number | null`, default `null`. How much is done, out of max. Without it, the bar is indeterminate.
- `max` (attribute `max`): `number`, default `100`. The value of a finished task.
- `tone` (attribute `tone`): `'accent' | 'ok' | 'warn' | 'danger'`, default `'accent'`. The colour of the bar.
- `size` (attribute `size`): `'sm' | 'md'`, default `'md'`. 8 or 4 pixels high.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. Above the bar, at the start; also its name for screen readers.
- `showValue` (attribute `show-value`): `boolean`, default `false`. Prints the percentage above the bar, at the end.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The label, the percentage and the bar.
- `--height` (custom property): The height of the bar.
- `--color` (custom property): The colour of the bar, beyond the tones.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Values

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-progress value="20"></jl-progress>
  <jl-progress value="55"></jl-progress>
  <jl-progress value="100" tone="ok"></jl-progress>
</div>
```

### Label and value

The label above at the start, the percentage at the end.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-progress label="Uploading report.pdf" value="64" show-value></jl-progress>
  <jl-progress label="Storage" value="9.1" max="10" tone="warn" show-value></jl-progress>
  <jl-progress label="API quota" value="98" tone="danger" show-value></jl-progress>
</div>
```

### Indeterminate

No value: work of unknown length.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-progress label="Preparing the export"></jl-progress>
  <jl-progress size="sm"></jl-progress>
</div>
```

### Sizes

sm is 4 pixels high, for a card or a table row; md is 8.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-progress size="sm" value="40"></jl-progress>
  <jl-progress value="40"></jl-progress>
</div>
```

### From code

The value set from code as the work advances.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <jl-progress class="demo-upload" label="Uploading 12 files" value="0" show-value></jl-progress>
  <div class="row"><jl-button class="demo-start" icon="upload" label="Start upload"></jl-button></div>
</div>
```

```js
const progress = root.querySelector('.demo-upload');
const start = root.querySelector('.demo-start');
start.events.register('press', () => {
  progress.value.set(0);
  progress.tone.set('accent');
  const timer = setInterval(() => {
    const next = Math.min(100, (progress.value.get() ?? 0) + 8);
    progress.value.set(next);
    if (next === 100) {
      clearInterval(timer);
      progress.tone.set('ok');
    }
  }, 200);
});
```
